title: TAMIU to Host Poetry Reading on the Cultural Heritage of the Americas with Carlos Aguasaco
excerpt: Texas A&M International University will host a reading from “Breviary of Americanisms” on Thursday, Nov. 19, with Colombian American poet Carlos Aguasaco and translator Jennifer Rathbun.
content:
Texas A&M International University will host a reading from “Breviary of Americanisms,” a new bilingual Spanish-English poetry collection by Colombian American poet and scholar Carlos Aguasaco, on Thursday, Nov. 19, from noon to 1 p.m. in Room 128 of the University’s Academic Innovation Center, according to TAMIU. Admission is free and open to the campus community and the public.

The collection, translated into English by Jennifer Rathbun, TAMIU associate dean of the College of Arts and Sciences and professor of Spanish, was published Oct. 21, 2026, by Broken Bowl Books, a division of Vaso Roto Ediciones.

The book recovers words and traditions rooted in the African and Indigenous origins of Latin America — including those of the Kuna, Incan, Mayan, Nahua, Bantu and Taíno peoples — arranged alphabetically, in the manner of dictionary definitions. Its form draws on the dictionary; its theme draws on the breviary, the traditional book of prayers, hymns, psalms and readings. Together, TAMIU said, the collection explores cultural memory, the reclamation of cultural identity and the recovery of histories that have often been marginalized or erased.

The reading marks a long-running collaboration: “Breviary of Americanisms” is Rathbun’s 20th poetry book in translation and her 24th book overall, and her second full-length collaboration with Aguasaco. The two have presented their work at institutions and literary conferences in Europe and the Americas, including the Instituto Cervantes and the Association of Writers and Writing Programs Annual Conference.

Aguasaco is a professor of Latin American Cultural Studies and chair of the Department of Interdisciplinary Arts & Sciences at The City College of the City University of New York. He received the Juan Felipe Herrera Award for “The New York City Subway Poems / Poemas del metro de Nueva York,” and his collection “Cardinal in My Window with a Mask on Its Beak,” translated by Rathbun, received the Academy of American Poets’ Ambroggio Prize. He is also the founder of Artepoetica Press and The Americas Poetry Festival of New York.

Rathbun’s publications include the poetry collections “Precipicio / Precipice” (2023) and “El libro de traiciones / The Book of Betrayals” (2021), and two edited anthologies featuring more than 50 authors whose work denounces femicide along the U.S.-Mexico border. Her most recent book, “Amherst Suite: Emily Dickinson, Spanish Translation and Poetic Transcreation,” was published by Amherst College Press in 2026.

For more information, TAMIU directs readers to the University’s College of Arts and Sciences at 956-326-2462 or coas@tamiu.edu.

Source: Texas A&M International University, “TAMIU to host poetry reading and discussion on cultural heritage of the Americas with award-winning poet Carlos Aguasaco,” Nov. 13, 2026. tamiu.edu
